messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] parallel computing in Stan
parts:
We haven't worked on parallelization of the log density
calculations. The tricky part is dealing with autodiff.

I take it you mean the .hpp file that gets generated for a model?

From what I gather from this:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenMP

I think you'd actually need to add some explicit parallelism
constructs to the program. We don't know how to do that with
autodiff.

If you have matrix operations and Eigen would use OpenMP somehow,
then there could be some gain. See:

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/TopicMultiThreading.html

But I'm not sure how to control it. The autodiff code cannot be
run in parallel because we don't have any locking mechanism in
place, so there would be both race conditions leading to memory
conflicts and also ordering issues that wouldn't be resolved.

If you do manage to get some speedup, we'd love to hear about
it and would write it up in the next version of the manual.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: parallel computing in Stan
parts:
I don't know what it'll do.

You just have to be careful that none of the matrix operators
working on var objects directly use parallelization. Anything
working on just double values could be parallelized.

For anything else, the code would have to be explicitly
instrumented to allow parallelization, which is very tricky with
the way autodiff works --- tricky enough we don't know how to
do it.

- Bob
